notes.sowing: Sow directly in spring once the soil has begun to warm, {cm:1} deep, and thin to {cm:30} to {cm:50} apart. Borage has a taproot and does not transplant well.
notes.care: Grows in most well-drained soils in sun; plants are smaller in dry, poor soil. Tall plants may lean, and grouping them helps them hold each other up. Bees visit the flowers heavily. It self-sows freely, so pull unwanted seedlings while small.
notes.harvest: Flowers start about 8 weeks from sowing and continue through summer, fading by late summer on spring-sown plants. Pick the blue flowers just as they open for salads and drinks.
